notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My first attempt to fetch the six main source pages hit a bug in my own code. The tool then refused any more calls, so I never saw any page content. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written anything about the verses rather than make it up.

These are the pages I tried to load, which would be the main sources if you start a new request:

- Enduring Word (Pentecostal and charismatic, verse by verse): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jeremiah-15/
- Precept Austin (evangelical): https://www.preceptaustin.org/jeremiah-15-commentary
- Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/jeremiah/15.htm
- Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/jeremiah/15.htm
- Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/jeremiah/15.htm
- NET Bible notes (modern scholarship): https://netbible.org/bible/Jeremiah+15

To cover the rest of your request, the next step would be searching the tradition-specific sites. That means Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu (Methodist), Spurgeon and Desiring God (Baptist), Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition (Reformed), LCMS and 1517 (Lutheran), and New Advent's Church Fathers and Haydock commentary (Catholic and Orthodox). The verses most worth checking there are:

- **vv. 1 and 4:** about prayer for others and Manasseh's guilt
- **vv. 11–14:** a famously hard passage to translate
- **v. 16:** "Your words were found, and I ate them"
- **vv. 18–19:** Jeremiah's complaint and God's call for him to return

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll fetch these pages one by one and write the verse-by-verse notes with a URL for every point.
